  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "T.CONN-SYN-SENT",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.10.7.3",
      "interpretation": "Validate ACK before processing SYN/RST; valid SYN+ACK establishes, bare SYN enters SYN-RECEIVED.",
      "kind": "protocol_interpretation",
      "strength": "algorithm"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.RTO-PROFILE",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6298.html#section-5",
      "interpretation": "Use 1000ms initial SYN RTO and exponential doubling for control retransmission. After a SYN timeout use at least 3000ms for subsequent FIN, retaining a larger backed-off value; no RTT estimator is modeled.",
      "kind": "profile_choice",
      "strength": "mixed"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-PROFILE",
      "source": "docs/tcp-wire-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Admission and failure order",
      "interpretation": "Finite raw IPv4 TCP wire transport of unchanged tcp-data protocol state/actions; unsupported domain remains model_gap. Drops modify only wire disposition."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-IP",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1",
      "interpretation": "Explicit fixed IPv4 layout, Total Length and header checksum; atomic ID0 output/any input ID within RFC6864 profile."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-TCP",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1 Header Format",
      "interpretation": "Explicit sequence/ack/window/flags, Data Offset, checksum and pseudoheader, with only declared fixed option shapes."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-MSS",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.7.1",
      "section": "3.7.1",
      "interpretation": "SYNACK may carry only kind2,length4,MSS>=4; existing SMSS4 output remains at or below offered MSS; no negotiation/storage fork."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-PUSH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.9.1.2",
      "section": "3.9.1.2 MUST60/MUST61; 3.9.1.3 MAY17",
      "interpretation": "Profile sends every nonempty segment with PSHACK and accepts ACK/PSHACK data through the same original byte/sequence rules; receive API does not expose optional PUSH flag. Explicit flush service remains an environment scheduling contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "CROSS-IP-LINK",
      "source": "docs/tcp-ipv4-endpoint.md",
      "kind": "modeling_choice",
      "interpretation": "finite explicit automatic ARP and shared latest raw IP pending slot; not an RFC mandated queue policy"
    },
    {
      "id": "VIRTUAL-ETHERNET-RX",
      "source": "docs/tcp-ipv4-virtual-link.md",
      "section": "Specification and observation / Acceptance boundary",
      "interpretation": "Finite virtual Ethernet receive service boundary admits exact IPv4 extent or canonical padding; physical TX padding and every other protocol guard/action are unchanged."
    }
  ]
}

  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "T.DATA-SEND",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.9.1.2",
      "interpretation": "Model buffers application octets and segments them within the configured capacity, MSS and send window.",
      "category": "protocol_behavior",
      "strength": "modeled_subset"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.DATA-WINDOW",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.10.7.4",
      "interpretation": "Update SND.WND only for acceptable ACK and newer WL1/WL2. Segmentation respects the available advertised send window.",
      "category": "protocol_behavior",
      "strength": "modeled_subset"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.DATA-SEQ",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.4",
      "interpretation": "Each new data octet consumes one sequence number; cumulative ACK removes an acknowledged prefix. Retransmission does not advance SND.NXT.",
      "category": "protocol_behavior",
      "strength": "modeled_subset"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.DATA-RTO",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6298.html#section-5",
      "interpretation": "Start on first outstanding transmission, restart on new partial ACK, cancel on all acknowledged, retransmit oldest on expiry and double RTO (5.1-5.6). No RTT sampling or maximum retry policy.",
      "category": "algorithm_subset",
      "strength": "modeled_subset"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-PROFILE",
      "source": "docs/tcp-wire-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Admission and failure order",
      "interpretation": "Finite raw IPv4 TCP wire transport of unchanged tcp-data protocol state/actions; unsupported domain remains model_gap. Drops modify only wire disposition."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-IP",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1",
      "interpretation": "Explicit fixed IPv4 layout, Total Length and header checksum; atomic ID0 output/any input ID within RFC6864 profile."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-TCP",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1 Header Format",
      "interpretation": "Explicit sequence/ack/window/flags, Data Offset, checksum and pseudoheader, with only declared fixed option shapes."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-MSS",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.7.1",
      "section": "3.7.1",
      "interpretation": "SYNACK may carry only kind2,length4,MSS>=4; existing SMSS4 output remains at or below offered MSS; no negotiation/storage fork."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-PUSH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.9.1.2",
      "section": "3.9.1.2 MUST60/MUST61; 3.9.1.3 MAY17",
      "interpretation": "Profile sends every nonempty segment with PSHACK and accepts ACK/PSHACK data through the same original byte/sequence rules; receive API does not expose optional PUSH flag. Explicit flush service remains an environment scheduling contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "CROSS-IP-LINK",
      "source": "docs/tcp-ipv4-endpoint.md",
      "kind": "modeling_choice",
      "interpretation": "finite explicit automatic ARP and shared latest raw IP pending slot; not an RFC mandated queue policy"
    }
  ]
}

  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "T.DATA-ACK",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.10.7.4",
      "interpretation": "New ACKs satisfy SND.UNA < SEG.ACK <= SND.NXT; duplicate and old ACKs do not remove data; future ACK triggers an ACK.",
      "category": "protocol_behavior",
      "strength": "modeled_subset"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.DATA-WINDOW",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.10.7.4",
      "interpretation": "Update SND.WND only for acceptable ACK and newer WL1/WL2. Segmentation respects the available advertised send window.",
      "category": "protocol_behavior",
      "strength": "modeled_subset"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.DATA-SEQ",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.4",
      "interpretation": "Each new data octet consumes one sequence number; cumulative ACK removes an acknowledged prefix. Retransmission does not advance SND.NXT.",
      "category": "protocol_behavior",
      "strength": "modeled_subset"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.DATA-RTO",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6298.html#section-5",
      "interpretation": "Start on first outstanding transmission, restart on new partial ACK, cancel on all acknowledged, retransmit oldest on expiry and double RTO (5.1-5.6). No RTT sampling or maximum retry policy.",
      "category": "algorithm_subset",
      "strength": "modeled_subset"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-PROFILE",
      "source": "docs/tcp-wire-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Admission and failure order",
      "interpretation": "Finite raw IPv4 TCP wire transport of unchanged tcp-data protocol state/actions; unsupported domain remains model_gap. Drops modify only wire disposition."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-IP",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1",
      "interpretation": "Explicit fixed IPv4 layout, Total Length and header checksum; atomic ID0 output/any input ID within RFC6864 profile."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-TCP",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1 Header Format",
      "interpretation": "Explicit sequence/ack/window/flags, Data Offset, checksum and pseudoheader, with only declared fixed option shapes."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-MSS",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.7.1",
      "section": "3.7.1",
      "interpretation": "SYNACK may carry only kind2,length4,MSS>=4; existing SMSS4 output remains at or below offered MSS; no negotiation/storage fork."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-PUSH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.9.1.2",
      "section": "3.9.1.2 MUST60/MUST61; 3.9.1.3 MAY17",
      "interpretation": "Profile sends every nonempty segment with PSHACK and accepts ACK/PSHACK data through the same original byte/sequence rules; receive API does not expose optional PUSH flag. Explicit flush service remains an environment scheduling contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "CROSS-IP-LINK",
      "source": "docs/tcp-ipv4-endpoint.md",
      "kind": "modeling_choice",
      "interpretation": "finite explicit automatic ARP and shared latest raw IP pending slot; not an RFC mandated queue policy"
    },
    {
      "id": "VIRTUAL-ETHERNET-RX",
      "source": "docs/tcp-ipv4-virtual-link.md",
      "section": "Specification and observation / Acceptance boundary",
      "interpretation": "Finite virtual Ethernet receive service boundary admits exact IPv4 extent or canonical padding; physical TX padding and every other protocol guard/action are unchanged."
    }
  ]
}

    {
      "id": "T.DATA-RECEIVE",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.10.7.4",
      "interpretation": "Accept and trim text overlapping the receive window; advance RCV.NXT only over contiguous newly accepted bytes, ACK the next expected octet.",
      "category": "protocol_behavior",
      "strength": "modeled_subset"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.DATA-SEQ",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.4",
      "interpretation": "Each new data octet consumes one sequence number; cumulative ACK removes an acknowledged prefix. Retransmission does not advance SND.NXT.",
      "category": "protocol_behavior",
      "strength": "modeled_subset"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.DATA-SCOPE",
      "source": "docs/tcp-data.md",
      "interpretation": "Finite single-connection profile, 16-byte send and receive capacity, MSS=4, handshake-advertised peer window, immediate ACK and explicit flush scheduler. Future/out-of-order data discarded without reassembly. Close requires buffers drained. No implementation conformance claim.",
      "category": "environment_assumption",
      "strength": "profile_choice"
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-PROFILE",
      "source": "docs/tcp-wire-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Admission and failure order",
      "interpretation": "Finite raw IPv4 TCP wire transport of unchanged tcp-data protocol state/actions; unsupported domain remains model_gap. Drops modify only wire disposition."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-IP",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1",
      "interpretation": "Explicit fixed IPv4 layout, Total Length and header checksum; atomic ID0 output/any input ID within RFC6864 profile."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-TCP",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1 Header Format",
      "interpretation": "Explicit sequence/ack/window/flags, Data Offset, checksum and pseudoheader, with only declared fixed option shapes."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-MSS",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.7.1",
      "section": "3.7.1",
      "interpretation": "SYNACK may carry only kind2,length4,MSS>=4; existing SMSS4 output remains at or below offered MSS; no negotiation/storage fork."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-PUSH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.9.1.2",
      "section": "3.9.1.2 MUST60/MUST61; 3.9.1.3 MAY17",
      "interpretation": "Profile sends every nonempty segment with PSHACK and accepts ACK/PSHACK data through the same original byte/sequence rules; receive API does not expose optional PUSH flag. Explicit flush service remains an environment scheduling contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "CROSS-IP-LINK",
      "source": "docs/tcp-ipv4-endpoint.md",
      "kind": "modeling_choice",
      "interpretation": "finite explicit automatic ARP and shared latest raw IP pending slot; not an RFC mandated queue policy"
    },
    {
      "id": "VIRTUAL-ETHERNET-RX",
      "source": "docs/tcp-ipv4-virtual-link.md",
      "section": "Specification and observation / Acceptance boundary",
      "interpretation": "Finite virtual Ethernet receive service boundary admits exact IPv4 extent or canonical padding; physical TX padding and every other protocol guard/action are unchanged."
    }
  ]
}

      "section": "3.1",
      "interpretation": "Explicit fixed IPv4 layout, Total Length and header checksum; atomic ID0 output/any input ID within RFC6864 profile."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-TCP",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1 Header Format",
      "interpretation": "Explicit sequence/ack/window/flags, Data Offset, checksum and pseudoheader, with only declared fixed option shapes."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-MSS",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.7.1",
      "section": "3.7.1",
      "interpretation": "SYNACK may carry only kind2,length4,MSS>=4; existing SMSS4 output remains at or below offered MSS; no negotiation/storage fork."
    },
    {
      "id": "T.WIRE-PUSH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293#section-3.9.1.2",
      "section": "3.9.1.2 MUST60/MUST61; 3.9.1.3 MAY17",
      "interpretation": "Profile sends every nonempty segment with PSHACK and accepts ACK/PSHACK data through the same original byte/sequence rules; receive API does not expose optional PUSH flag. Explicit flush service remains an environment scheduling contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "CROSS-IP-LINK",
      "source": "docs/tcp-ipv4-endpoint.md",
      "kind": "modeling_choice",
      "interpretation": "finite explicit automatic ARP and shared latest raw IP pending slot; not an RFC mandated queue policy"
    }
  ]
}

  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-RX-PROFILE",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Preserve existing raw component policy within explicitly checked fixed Ethernet ingress envelope; independent module variables; three inherited ARP states."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-UDP-LENGTH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc768",
      "section": "Fields pp1-2",
      "interpretation": "UDP length includes eight-byte header and data; surplus beyond UDP length remains out of scope."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-UDP-CHECKSUM",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122#section-4.1.3.4",
      "section": "4.1.3.4",
      "interpretation": "Discard invalid nonzero checksum; optionally discard absent checksum. This profile defaults to allowing absent checksums."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-UDP-PSEUDO",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc768",
      "section": "Fields p2",
      "interpretation": "Checksum covers pseudoheader with IP addresses/protocol/UDP length plus UDP header/data. Zero means absent; FFFF validates normally."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-IP-ATOMIC-ID",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6864#section-4.1",
      "section": "4/4.1 Atomic datagrams",
      "interpretation": "Only DF1/MF0/offset0 packets: ignore arbitrary ID for admission/duplicate semantics; original ID octets remain checked by the IPv4 checksum."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-INGRESS",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Finite fixed-link profile; full frame bounds/canonical padding checked before raw IP slice; ingress does not learn ARP or alter queued TX."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-LINK",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc894",
      "section": "Frame Format; verified erratum570",
      "interpretation": "Ethernet IPv4 type0800; padding excluded from IP length/checksum. Canonical extent is finite profile policy, arbitrary input pad ignored and output zero padded."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-INTERFACE",
      "source": "https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/tree/Documentation/networking/tuntap.rst?h=v6.12",
      "section": "1 Description; 3 Program interface",
      "interpretation": "Pinned v6.12 TUN/TAP document describes userspace replacement of physical media and TAP Ethernet frame I/O; it does not mandate padding behavior or prove a runner kernel implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-EXTENT",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-tap.md",
      "section": "Exact ingress extent",
      "interpretation": "Declared finite interface union: exactly14+IPtotal or canonical max60 extent; no adapter normalization; malformed Total Length drops before any extraction, partial padding remains gap. Original canonical module unchanged."
    }
  ]
}

  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-RX-PROFILE",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Preserve existing raw component policy within explicitly checked fixed Ethernet ingress envelope; independent module variables; three inherited ARP states."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-UDP-LENGTH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc768",
      "section": "Fields pp1-2",
      "interpretation": "UDP length includes eight-byte header and data; surplus beyond UDP length remains out of scope."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-UDP-CHECKSUM",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122#section-4.1.3.4",
      "section": "4.1.3.4",
      "interpretation": "Discard invalid nonzero checksum; optionally discard absent checksum. This profile defaults to allowing absent checksums."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-UDP-PSEUDO",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc768",
      "section": "Fields p2",
      "interpretation": "Checksum covers pseudoheader with IP addresses/protocol/UDP length plus UDP header/data. Zero means absent; FFFF validates normally."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-IP-ATOMIC-ID",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6864#section-4.1",
      "section": "4/4.1 Atomic datagrams",
      "interpretation": "Only DF1/MF0/offset0 packets: ignore arbitrary ID for admission/duplicate semantics; original ID octets remain checked by the IPv4 checksum."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-INGRESS",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Finite fixed-link profile; full frame bounds/canonical padding checked before raw IP slice; ingress does not learn ARP or alter queued TX."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-LINK",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc894",
      "section": "Frame Format; verified erratum570",
      "interpretation": "Ethernet IPv4 type0800; padding excluded from IP length/checksum. Canonical extent is finite profile policy, arbitrary input pad ignored and output zero padded."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-INTERFACE",
      "source": "https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/tree/Documentation/networking/tuntap.rst?h=v6.12",
      "section": "1 Description; 3 Program interface",
      "interpretation": "Pinned v6.12 TUN/TAP document describes userspace replacement of physical media and TAP Ethernet frame I/O; it does not mandate padding behavior or prove a runner kernel implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-EXTENT",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-tap.md",
      "section": "Exact ingress extent",
      "interpretation": "Declared finite interface union: exactly14+IPtotal or canonical max60 extent; no adapter normalization; malformed Total Length drops before any extraction, partial padding remains gap. Original canonical module unchanged."
    }
  ]
}

  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-RX-PROFILE",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Preserve existing raw component policy within explicitly checked fixed Ethernet ingress envelope; independent module variables; three inherited ARP states."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-UDP-LENGTH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc768",
      "section": "Fields pp1-2",
      "interpretation": "UDP length includes eight-byte header and data; surplus beyond UDP length remains out of scope."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-UDP-CHECKSUM",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122#section-4.1.3.4",
      "section": "4.1.3.4",
      "interpretation": "Discard invalid nonzero checksum; optionally discard absent checksum. This profile defaults to allowing absent checksums."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-UDP-PSEUDO",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc768",
      "section": "Fields p2",
      "interpretation": "Checksum covers pseudoheader with IP addresses/protocol/UDP length plus UDP header/data. Zero means absent; FFFF validates normally."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.UDPRX-IP-ATOMIC-ID",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6864#section-4.1",
      "section": "4/4.1 Atomic datagrams",
      "interpretation": "Only DF1/MF0/offset0 packets: ignore arbitrary ID for admission/duplicate semantics; original ID octets remain checked by the IPv4 checksum."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-INGRESS",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Finite fixed-link profile; full frame bounds/canonical padding checked before raw IP slice; ingress does not learn ARP or alter queued TX."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-LINK",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc894",
      "section": "Frame Format; verified erratum570",
      "interpretation": "Ethernet IPv4 type0800; padding excluded from IP length/checksum. Canonical extent is finite profile policy, arbitrary input pad ignored and output zero padded."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-INTERFACE",
      "source": "https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/tree/Documentation/networking/tuntap.rst?h=v6.12",
      "section": "1 Description; 3 Program interface",
      "interpretation": "Pinned v6.12 TUN/TAP document describes userspace replacement of physical media and TAP Ethernet frame I/O; it does not mandate padding behavior or prove a runner kernel implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-EXTENT",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-tap.md",
      "section": "Exact ingress extent",
      "interpretation": "Declared finite interface union: exactly14+IPtotal or canonical max60 extent; no adapter normalization; malformed Total Length drops before any extraction, partial padding remains gap. Original canonical module unchanged."
    }
  ]
}

  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ECHO-REPLY",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc792",
      "section": "Echo or Echo Reply pp14-15",
      "interpretation": "Reverse addresses, type0/code0, unchanged identifier/sequence and all data; recompute checksum including odd zero pad for arithmetic only."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ECHO-HOST",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122#section-3.2.2.6",
      "section": "3.2.2.6",
      "interpretation": "Echo server and same specific-destination source/data preservation, within declared unicast profile only."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ICMP-CHECKSUM",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc792",
      "section": "Echo Checksum p14",
      "interpretation": "Validate ones-complement checksum over complete ICMP message; no UDP absent/zero remapping. Invalid admitted message silently discarded by profile policy."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-IP-LENGTH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1 Total Length",
      "interpretation": "Exact raw datagram length in this nonfragmented IHL5 profile."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-IP-ATOMIC",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6864#section-4.1",
      "section": "4/4.1 Atomic datagrams",
      "interpretation": "DF1/MF0/off0: input ID ignored for semantics but checked by checksum; output atomic ID0 profile choice."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ECHO-PROFILE",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Preserve existing raw component policy within explicitly checked fixed Ethernet ingress envelope; independent module variables; three inherited ARP states."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-INGRESS",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Finite fixed-link profile; full frame bounds/canonical padding checked before raw IP slice; ingress does not learn ARP or alter queued TX."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-LINK",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc894",
      "section": "Frame Format; verified erratum570",
      "interpretation": "Ethernet IPv4 type0800; padding excluded from IP length/checksum. Canonical extent is finite profile policy, arbitrary input pad ignored and output zero padded."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-INTERFACE",
      "source": "https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/tree/Documentation/networking/tuntap.rst?h=v6.12",
      "section": "1 Description; 3 Program interface",
      "interpretation": "Pinned v6.12 TUN/TAP document describes userspace replacement of physical media and TAP Ethernet frame I/O; it does not mandate padding behavior or prove a runner kernel implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-EXTENT",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-tap.md",
      "section": "Exact ingress extent",
      "interpretation": "Declared finite interface union: exactly14+IPtotal or canonical max60 extent; no adapter normalization; malformed Total Length drops before any extraction, partial padding remains gap. Original canonical module unchanged."
    }
  ]
}

  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ECHO-REPLY",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc792",
      "section": "Echo or Echo Reply pp14-15",
      "interpretation": "Reverse addresses, type0/code0, unchanged identifier/sequence and all data; recompute checksum including odd zero pad for arithmetic only."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ECHO-HOST",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122#section-3.2.2.6",
      "section": "3.2.2.6",
      "interpretation": "Echo server and same specific-destination source/data preservation, within declared unicast profile only."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ICMP-CHECKSUM",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc792",
      "section": "Echo Checksum p14",
      "interpretation": "Validate ones-complement checksum over complete ICMP message; no UDP absent/zero remapping. Invalid admitted message silently discarded by profile policy."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-IP-LENGTH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1 Total Length",
      "interpretation": "Exact raw datagram length in this nonfragmented IHL5 profile."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-IP-ATOMIC",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6864#section-4.1",
      "section": "4/4.1 Atomic datagrams",
      "interpretation": "DF1/MF0/off0: input ID ignored for semantics but checked by checksum; output atomic ID0 profile choice."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ECHO-PROFILE",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Preserve existing raw component policy within explicitly checked fixed Ethernet ingress envelope; independent module variables; three inherited ARP states."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-INGRESS",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Finite fixed-link profile; full frame bounds/canonical padding checked before raw IP slice; ingress does not learn ARP or alter queued TX."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-LINK",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc894",
      "section": "Frame Format; verified erratum570",
      "interpretation": "Ethernet IPv4 type0800; padding excluded from IP length/checksum. Canonical extent is finite profile policy, arbitrary input pad ignored and output zero padded."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-INTERFACE",
      "source": "https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/tree/Documentation/networking/tuntap.rst?h=v6.12",
      "section": "1 Description; 3 Program interface",
      "interpretation": "Pinned v6.12 TUN/TAP document describes userspace replacement of physical media and TAP Ethernet frame I/O; it does not mandate padding behavior or prove a runner kernel implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-EXTENT",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-tap.md",
      "section": "Exact ingress extent",
      "interpretation": "Declared finite interface union: exactly14+IPtotal or canonical max60 extent; no adapter normalization; malformed Total Length drops before any extraction, partial padding remains gap. Original canonical module unchanged."
    }
  ]
}

  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ECHO-REPLY",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc792",
      "section": "Echo or Echo Reply pp14-15",
      "interpretation": "Reverse addresses, type0/code0, unchanged identifier/sequence and all data; recompute checksum including odd zero pad for arithmetic only."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ECHO-HOST",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122#section-3.2.2.6",
      "section": "3.2.2.6",
      "interpretation": "Echo server and same specific-destination source/data preservation, within declared unicast profile only."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ICMP-CHECKSUM",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc792",
      "section": "Echo Checksum p14",
      "interpretation": "Validate ones-complement checksum over complete ICMP message; no UDP absent/zero remapping. Invalid admitted message silently discarded by profile policy."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-IP-LENGTH",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791#section-3.1",
      "section": "3.1 Total Length",
      "interpretation": "Exact raw datagram length in this nonfragmented IHL5 profile."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-IP-ATOMIC",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6864#section-4.1",
      "section": "4/4.1 Atomic datagrams",
      "interpretation": "DF1/MF0/off0: input ID ignored for semantics but checked by checksum; output atomic ID0 profile choice."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ECHO-ECHO-PROFILE",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Preserve existing raw component policy within explicitly checked fixed Ethernet ingress envelope; independent module variables; three inherited ARP states."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-INGRESS",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-endpoint.md",
      "section": "Fixed version, sources and admission",
      "interpretation": "Finite fixed-link profile; full frame bounds/canonical padding checked before raw IP slice; ingress does not learn ARP or alter queued TX."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.ENDPOINT-LINK",
      "source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc894",
      "section": "Frame Format; verified erratum570",
      "interpretation": "Ethernet IPv4 type0800; padding excluded from IP length/checksum. Canonical extent is finite profile policy, arbitrary input pad ignored and output zero padded."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-INTERFACE",
      "source": "https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/tree/Documentation/networking/tuntap.rst?h=v6.12",
      "section": "1 Description; 3 Program interface",
      "interpretation": "Pinned v6.12 TUN/TAP document describes userspace replacement of physical media and TAP Ethernet frame I/O; it does not mandate padding behavior or prove a runner kernel implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "L.TAP-EXTENT",
      "source": "docs/ipv4-udp-icmp-tap.md",
      "section": "Exact ingress extent",
      "interpretation": "Declared finite interface union: exactly14+IPtotal or canonical max60 extent; no adapter normalization; malformed Total Length drops before any extraction, partial padding remains gap. Original canonical module unchanged."
    }
  ]
}
